steps.title: Why bands at all
steps.body: Saturating a full mix lets the loudest thing in it decide how everything else distorts. Bands stop the kick from choosing what the cymbals do.

steps.title: One to six
steps.body: Add a band and a new crossover appears. You can change this while audio is playing — the crossovers fade rather than click.

steps.title: Drag a crossover
steps.body: Hold Alt to snap to musical points, Cmd to move every edge together, Shift for fine control. Right-click the display to distribute them evenly.

steps.title: Solo to hear one band
steps.body: Solo is how you find out what a band is actually contributing. Most bands sound worse alone than they do in context, which is normal.

steps.title: Bypass to hear its absence
steps.body: A bypassed band still passes through with the same latency, so the sum does not comb. Comparing with and without is more informative than soloing.

steps.title: Linear phase, and when to want it
steps.body: Minimum phase is the default and costs no latency. Linear phase keeps the band edges phase-aligned, which matters when you are blending heavily with the dry signal — and costs latency, so it is a mixing choice, not a tracking one.
